# Neil Artus - Backend & AI Software Engineer

> I build distributed backend systems, applied AI, and cloud infrastructure. My work spans enterprise automation at Emerson and JG Summit, streaming research agents, and embedded AI prototypes. I focus on the systems behind the interface: APIs, data pipelines, authentication, and deployment.

Last updated: 2026-09-05. Biography and private-project descriptions are owner-provided. Public repository links document implementation details, not independently audited outcomes.

## Experience

- **AI Engineer Intern, Emerson** (March 2026 - July 2026): Developed AI-assisted cybersecurity compliance workflows, MCP integrations, and telemetry services for internal engineering teams.
- **AI Engineer Intern (GenAI Research), JG Summit Holdings Inc.** (June 2025 - August 2025): Developed a financial research and reporting application with Flask, React, Azure OpenAI, and LangChain for treasury and corporate strategy workflows.

## Projects

- [AGOS: Agentic Philippine Market Intelligence Platform](https://www.neilart.us/#agos): Philippine market research platform with a React interface, FastAPI services, and ingestion pipelines for market, economic, and news data.
- [Enterprise HR Automation Engine](https://www.neilart.us/#hr-automation): Python-based attendance reporting workflow with authenticated access to employee records.
- [MediSeen: Clinical Decision Support Platform](https://www.neilart.us/#mediseen): Clinical decision-support research prototype with a web interface and streamed AI responses.
- [CNN-Osteo: Thermal-Image Screening Prototype](https://www.neilart.us/#cnn-osteo): Research prototype using TensorFlow and MobileNetV3Small to classify thermal knee images into osteoarthritis-related categories, with Raspberry Pi as the deployment target.
- [AlerSense: Attention-Monitoring Prototype](https://www.neilart.us/#alersense): Demonstration prototype combining ESP32 telemetry, a Python video-inference component, a Flask-SocketIO API, and a Next.js dashboard.
- [DFA Visualizer: Formal Language Workbench](https://www.neilart.us/#dfa-visualizer): Browser-based React and TypeScript workbench for DFA simulation (automata and formal languages), right-linear grammar derivation, and derived PDA simulation.
